scam_flow: 1. Victim discovers phishing domain (via Telegram channels, romance scams, or search ads)
2. Phishing site mimics Trust Wallet multi-chain interface
3. Victim creates/imports wallet — mnemonic and password captured by backend
4. sessionLogin generated client-side (62^25 keyspace), sent to server
5. Wallet appears functional — balances shown, staking pools displayed
6. When victim attempts withdrawal, transaction 'fails' or is 'blocked'
7. Live chat support activates — operator impersonates Trust Wallet Support
8. Operator claims assets frozen due to 'OFAC sanctions', 'AML violations', or 'wrong network'
9. Victim told to deposit equivalent amount for 'asset replacement from common pool'
10. If victim pays, operator demands additional deposits (repeat extraction)
11. If victim refuses, operator threatens 'OFAC jurisdiction transfer' with deadlines
12. Stolen funds moved through rotating ETH/TRON/BTC addresses
